recorded.pass:q-foreach-fourth-of-five: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-foreach-fourth-of-five: Page decides b by its four-element case generalised to five: "removing B1 shrinks the list to three, and `hasNext()` only compares its position, 3, with the size, 3. The loop ends without calling `next()`, so nothing throws and B2 is never tested." Summary: "A for-each removal throws or silently skips the last element". The reader must carry the page's 4-element example to a 5-element list (position 4 vs size 4); the page does not state the general rule beyond this example.

recorded.outcome:q-removeif-copy:a: Refuted by "Whether the call is allowed at all is up to the list." and the table: List.copyOf, nothing matches -> `UnsupportedOperationException`; output line "List.of, nothing expired: java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException".
recorded.prompt:q-removeif-copy:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-removeif-copy:b: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-removeif-copy:b: Refuted: List.copyOf's removeIf "throws before testing a single element" (a removal call, not an add), and Arrays.asList refuses removal too: "Arrays.asList, one expired: java.lang.UnsupportedOperationException: remove". Minor: the option's 'says' claims every mutator on List.copyOf throws; the page attributes "every mutator throws" to the List.of javadoc and states only removeIf for List.copyOf.

recorded.outcome:q-removeif-copy:d: Refuted by "throws before testing a single element"; Design Note: the collection decides "whether it runs at all, as `List.of` does when it throws before calling it".
